reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No direct target engagement data reported for PLK1 or AR. PSA levels were measured but specific values not provided. PSA measurement suggests some pathway monitoring but results not detailed. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (disease control at 12 weeks) was met overall at 29.2%, but individual arms showed variable responses (13.6%, 35%, 35.7%). This suggests partial efficacy with dose-dependent effects across the three arms. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. All arms treated the same metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer population. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This is a dose-escalation study without a control arm, making it difficult to attribute efficacy definitively to the combination. Safety signals including DLTs and grade ≥3 TEAEs were common, potentially limiting optimal dosing.
